title: Throughput-aware preemptive scaling for maintenance windows
creator: Priya Anand
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets currently apply maintenance windows and node drains agnostic to live throughput guarantees. When maintenance begins we often see transient throughput drops or elevated tail latency unless teams pre-warm capacity manually. Goal: implement an automated, throughput-aware preemptive scaling and drain coordination system so maintenance events preserve per-customer throughput SLAs and minimize tail latency and request rejections.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane can schedule maintenance windows with a throughput SLA target per customer (requests/sec or tokens/sec)
Before a maintenance event, fleet autoscaler automatically computes and provisions temporary buffer capacity to preserve SLA within configured cost caps
Node draining is coordinated with live request routing so KV cache and streaming in-flight requests are gracefully handled without exceeding latency SLOs
Console exposes maintenance simulation preview (estimated cost, expected token throughput, risk window) and an "undo" pathway
End-to-end e2e test that simulates a 20% fleet maintenance window and demonstrates <5% throughput degradation for customers with SLA flags enabled
design_summary: We will introduce a Maintenance Orchestrator service that augments the existing autoscaler. Key pieces: 1) SLA profile per customer that expresses throughput targets and cost guardrails; 2) Predictive pre-scale estimator that uses recent token/sec rolling windows and model latency curves to compute required buffer VMs/GPUs; 3) Coordinated drain protocol that signals serving nodes to gracefully reject new cold-start requests while finishing hot KV cache handoffs and streaming completions; 4) Console UX to create, preview, and execute maintenance windows with per-customer impact forecasts.
implementation_plan: Schema: add 'maintenance_sla' to customer fleet config (throughput_target, cost_cap_pct, priority)
Autoscaler: extend decision loop to accept pre-scale adjustments from Maintenance Orchestrator and honor cost caps
Drain protocol: implement 3-phase drain (quiesce new long-lived streams; spill prefix cache to nearest warm node; final soft-evict) with new hooks in runtime
Simulator: lightweight maintenance simulation engine that runs against production traffic profiles for previews
Console: maintenance window creation UI, preview card, and API endpoint for programmatic scheduling
Telemetry: new metrics (maintenance_pre_scale_count, maintenance_pre_scale_cost, in_drain_inflight_tokens) and dashboard templates
E2E tests: chaos injection harness to validate throughput preservation under varying workloads and model sizes
rollout_strategy: Start with internal alpha on staging fleets (opt-in), then beta with a small set of pilot customers who have Dedicated reserved capacity. Monitor key metrics for two maintenance cycles before gradual enablement. Provide a manual override to disable pre-scaling per customer. Time-boxed automatic reversion if customer throughput degrades by >7% compared to baseline.
migration_notes: Existing fleets without maintenance_sla will continue to use current maintenance flow (no pre-scaling). We will provide a one-click migration script to populate maintenance_sla from historical throughput percentiles and current reserved capacity.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-provisioning increases customer cost unexpectedly. Mitigation: enforce 'cost_cap_pct' and conservative initial headroom, plus billing notice emails for pilot customers.
Risk: Incorrect pre-scale estimator for bursty workloads. Mitigation: fallback to conservative static headroom and require test simulation before scheduling.

Risk: Drain protocol complexity interacts with KV cache consistency. Mitigation: add invariant checks and telemetry for cache misses during/after drains and run canary experiments on read-heavy workloads.
open_questions: What default cost_cap_pct is acceptable across customer tiers (P0/P1 enterprise vs PLG free)?
Should maintenance pre-scaling be charged as ephemeral usage or amortized into reserved capacity calculations?
How does this integrate with cross-region fallback when capacity cannot be provisioned in the same region?
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for autoscaler hooks, integration tests for drain handshake, and a staged chaos runbook. We'll also produce a synthetic load replay using historical traffic traces to validate estimator accuracy. Performance regression tests must prove <3% added tail latency under nominal conditions.
observability: Add Grafana dashboards and alerting rules for maintenance_pre_scale_cost > cost_cap_pct, maintenance_event_failed_allocations > 0, and customer_sla_violation_count. Instrument sampling of per-request routing decisions during maintenance for postmortems.
privacy_compliance: No customer PII changes. Ensure audit logs record maintenance initiator, time window, and pre-scale actions for compliance teams.
dependencies_notes: Depends on runtime drain hooks (ENG-31627) and predictive decommission heuristics (ENG-28341). Also coordinates with console team for UX widgets.
